newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rice export prices seen mixed.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rice export prices seen mixed.

text.p: Pakistani rice export prices are likely to remain mixed next week on low exports before the 1997/98 (July-June) budget, dealers said on Thursday.
Exporters are awaiting the budget announcement, expected on June 14, before finalising contracts, they said.
Khalid Ghori of Matco Rice Processing said basmati export prices were falling on low demand from abroad but IRRI-6 prices were rising on tight supplies of good-quality rice for export.

The state-run Rice Export Corporation is expected to take a decision on three bids for the sale and export of 5,000 tonnes of basmati variety Pak-7 1996/97 (July-June) rice, containing seven percent broken, in the next day or two.
An official said the highest bid was $436 per tonne FOB, with the others at $435.10 and $425. Bids were opened on May 26.
Pakistan exported 1.571 million tonnes of rice worth $393 million in the first 10 months of 1996/97 compared to 1.133 million worth $372 million in the same period a year ago.
In April, rice exports fell to 180,094 tonnes worth $48 million compared to 372,828 tonnes worth $62 million in March and 118,141 tonnes worth $38 million in April 1996.
